title: by
subtitle: by car / by chance / a book by ...
summary: Use by to say how something happens, how you travel, who did something, what is next to you, and how big a difference is.

lesson.heading: by chance, by mistake
lesson.text: Something can happen **by mistake / by accident / by chance**. In these expressions we use **by + noun** with no *the* or *a*. But if you mean to do something, you do it **on purpose**.

examples.text: We hadn't arranged to meet. We met **by chance**.
I didn't do it **on purpose**. It was an accident.

lesson.heading: by car, by bus
lesson.text: We use **by** to say how somebody travels: by car, by train, by plane, by boat, by ship, by bus, by bike. But we usually say **on foot**.

examples.text: Jess usually goes to work **by bus** / **by bike** / **by car**.
Did you come here **by car** or **on foot**?

lesson.heading: by car, but in my car
lesson.text: We do not use **by** if we say *my car / the train / a taxi*. We use **in** for cars and taxis, and **on** for bikes and public transport.

right.label: in / on with my, the, a ...
examples: They didn't come **in their car**. They came **in a taxi**.
We travelled **on the 6.45 train**, which arrived at 8.30.

lesson.heading: Other ways of doing things
lesson.text: We also use **by** to say how we do other things: send something **by post**, pay **by card** or **by cheque**, do something **by hand**.

examples.text: Don't put my sweater in the washing machine. It has to be washed **by hand**.

lesson.note: But we say **pay cash** or **pay in cash**, not usually *by cash*.

lesson.heading: by or with?
lesson.text: In passive sentences the person or thing that does the action comes after **by**. The tool or instrument that is used comes after **with**.

left.label: by = who or what did it
examples: Have you ever been bitten **by a dog**?
The programme was watched **by millions of people**.
The door must have been opened **by somebody with a key**.

right.label: with = the thing used
examples: The door must have been opened **with a key**.
We managed to put the fire out **with a fire extinguisher**.

lesson.note: We also say a play **by** Shakespeare, a painting **by** Rembrandt, a novel **by** Tolstoy: 'Who is this painting **by**? Picasso?'

lesson.heading: by = next to; by = the difference
lesson.text: **By** can also mean *next to / beside*. And we use **by** to show the difference between two amounts.

examples.text: The light switch is **by the door**.
Clare's salary has increased **by ten per cent**.
examples.note: = it's now ten per cent more than before

examples.text: Carl won the race **by five metres**.
examples.note: = he was five metres in front of the other runners

lesson.text: Remember the pattern: by + bare noun (by car, by chance, by hand), but in/on + my/the/a (in my car, on the train).

exercises.prompt: We don't need cash. We can pay ___.
exercises.explanation: We pay by card, by cheque or by credit card.

exercises.prompt: I didn't intend to take your umbrella. I took it ___.
exercises.explanation: By mistake, by accident, by chance - no the or a after by.

exercises.prompt: I think he arrived late ___. He wanted to keep us waiting.
exercises.explanation: If you mean to do something, you do it on purpose.

exercises.prompt: I saw Jane this morning. She was ___ the bus.
exercises.explanation: By bus, but on the bus - we use on with the/my/a and public transport.

exercises.prompt: How did you get here? Did you come ___?
exercises.explanation: By + the means of transport on its own: by train, by car, by plane.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition do we use with each phrase?
We travelled ___ because it is larger and more comfortable than mine.
exercises.explanation: With my/the/a we use in for cars and taxis, not by.

exercises.statement: He doesn't drive much. He goes everywhere by bike or by foot.
exercises.explanation: He goes everywhere by bike or on foot. We say on foot, not by foot.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of the sentences.

pairs.left: We lost the game because of a mistake
I was woken up in the night

exercises.prompt: We managed to put the fire out ___ a fire extinguisher.
exercises.explanation: With is for the tool that is used; by is for the person or thing that does the action.

exercises.prompt: Who's that man standing ___ the window?
exercises.explanation: Here by means next to or beside.

exercises.prompt: Carl was five metres in front of the other runners, so Carl won the race ___.
exercises.explanation: By shows the size of the difference: won by five metres, increased by ten per cent.
